parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, border/facility/custody universal exposure, or documented targeting/violence against trans visitors is documented, and same-sex conduct is no longer criminalised—sexuality law is secondary. Absence of resident legal gender recognition is not itself a visitor exposure. If outed, however, severity is moderate: discrimination in hotels, transport, health and public accommodations is not illegal and no hate-crime or visitor remedy is documented. Social climate is hostile, not merely friction: religious/political leaders drive crackdowns on LGBTQ visibility, past police harassment of gay venues and a Pride arrest, only 5% support legal gender change and 69% in 2017 said same-sex relations should be criminalised. That is societal hostility with thin/no recourse, placing it in Elevated Risk below acceptance-with-working-protections jurisdictions, but above tiers with unremedied universal exclusion or organised targeting.
